ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་དགའ་བ་དང་། གསུང་གི་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་དགའ་བ་དང་། ཐུགས་ཀྱི་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་དགའ་བ་དང་། ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་དགའ་བ་སྟེ། དེ་ལྟར་དེ་ཉིད་རྣམ་པ་བཅུ་དྲུག་ནི་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་སྐུ་ཞེས་བརྗོད་པར་བྱ་ལ། དེ་ནས་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ་དེ་ནས་
ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུ་དང་དེ་ནས་སྤྲུལ་པའི་སྐུའོ། །དེ་བཞིན་དུ་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་གསུང་དང་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་ཐུགས་དང་། ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་དང་། ཆོས་ཀྱི་གསུང་དང་། ཆོས་ཀྱི་ཐུགས་དང་། ཆོས་ཀྱི་ཡེ་ཤེས་དང་། ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་གསུང་དང་། ལོངས་སྤྱོད་
རྫོགས་པའི་ཐུགས་དང་། ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་དང་། སྤྲུལ་པའི་གསུང་དང་། སྤྲུལ་པའི་ཐུགས་དང་། སྤྲུལ་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་སོ་ཞེས་སོ། །དེ་ལྟར་ཆ་བཅུ་དྲུག་གི་སྒྲིབ་པ་ཟད་པའི་ཕྱིར། རྡོ་རྗེ་ཟླ་བ་དྲི་མེད་འོད། །ཅེས་གྲུབ་བོ། །དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཟླ་བ་དྲི་མེད་འོད་ཉིད་ལས་སྲིད་མེད་
སྲིད་པ་སོང་བ་སྟེ། སྲིད་མེད་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་དང་སྲིད་པ་འཁོར་བ་ཡིན་ལ། དེ་དག་འཁོར་བ་སྤྲོ་བའི་རྒྱུ་ཅན་དག་སྟེ། དེ་དག་དང་བྲལ་བ་དེ་ལའོ། །དེའི་ཕྱིར་ཤེས་དང་ཤེས་བྱ་གཅིག་གྱུར་ཏེ། ཤེས་པ་འཁོར་བ་ལས་རྒལ་བར་མི་འགྱུར་བ་དང་། ཤེས་བྱ་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ་ལས་
ཀྱང་འདས་པའི་གཟུགས་ཏེ། དེ་དག་གིས་གཅིག་ཏུ་གྱུར་པ་ནི་རྟག་པ་དང་ཆད་པ་ལས་ངེས་པར་གྲོལ་བ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་དབྱེར་མེད་པའི་ངོ་བོའོ། །དེ་ཉིད་ཀྱི་ཕྱིར་ཡང་དག་པའི་སྦྱོར་བའི་ཚུལ་ལས་རྒྱལ་བ་མཆོག་གི་འདུས་པ་སྟེ་སྒྲིབ་པ་མེད་པའི་ཕུང་པོ་དང་། ཁམས་དང་དབང་པོ་ལ་
སོགས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་པའོ་ཞེས་པའོ། །རྣམ་པ་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་བདེན་དོན་ཞེས་པ་ལ་བདེན་དོན་ནི་དེ་ཁོ་ན་ཉིད་རིན་པོ་ཆེའོ། །དེ་ཡང་རྣམ་པ་བཅུ་གཉིས་སུ་དབྱེ་སྟེ། མ་རིག་པ་ལ་སོགས་པ་ཡན་ལག་བཅུ་གཉིས་སྲོག་ལ་སོགས་པ་རླུང་བཅུ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་ངོ་བོ་རྣམས་འགགས་པ་ཞེས་
པའོ། །རྩ་བའི་རྒྱུད་དུ་གསུངས་པ། སྲོག་ལ་སོགས་པ་རླུང་མ་དག །ཡན་ལག་བཅུ་གཉིས་རིགས་བྱུང་བ། །དེ་རྣམས་ཁྱིམ་དུ་ཡང་དག་བཤད། །དེ་རྣམས་ལ་ནི་གཟའ་རྣམས་འབྱུང་། །རྣམ་པ་བཅུ་གཉིས་འཁོར་ལོ་འདི། །ཡན་ལག་བཅུ་གཉིས་སྲིད་པར་བཤད། །ཡན་ལག་བཅུ་

...the joy of the innate <term>sahaja</term> <gloss>co-emergent or innate</gloss>, the joy of the innate speech, the joy of the innate mind, and the joy of the innate primordial wisdom. Thus, these sixteen aspects are called the Innate Body <term>Sahajakaya</term>. From that arises the Reality Body <term>Dharmakaya</term>, then the Enjoyment Body <term>Sambhogakaya</term>, and then the Emanation Body <term>Nirmanakaya</term>.

Similarly, there is the innate speech, the innate mind, and the innate primordial wisdom; the speech of reality, the mind of reality, and the primordial wisdom of reality; the enjoyment speech, the enjoyment mind, and the enjoyment primordial wisdom; and the emanation speech, the emanation mind, and the emanation primordial wisdom. Because the obscurations of these sixteen parts are exhausted, it is established as the Vajra Moon of Stainless Light <note>original: "Vajracandra Vimalaprabha"</note>.

For that reason, through the Vajra Moon of Stainless Light itself, one has moved beyond existence and non-existence. Non-existence refers to <term>Nirvana</term> <gloss>the state beyond suffering</gloss> and existence refers to <term>Samsara</term> <gloss>the cycle of birth and death</gloss>. These are caused by the proliferation of cyclic existence; the state is free from both. Therefore, the knower and the known become one. Consciousness does not cross over from cyclic existence, and the known is a form that even transcends <term>Nirvana</term>. Because they have become one, they are of an indivisible essence, being definitively liberated from the extremes of permanence and nihilism.

For that very reason, through the method of perfect union, there is the assembly of the Supreme Victors <note>original: "Jina"</note>, which is the collection of the stainless aggregates <term>skandhas</term>, elements <term>dhatus</term>, sense faculties <term>indriyas</term>, and so forth.

Regarding the phrase "the truth of the twelve aspects," the truth is the precious reality itself <term>tattva</term>. This is further divided into twelve aspects, which refers to the cessation of the twelve links of dependent origination <note>starting with ignorance</note> and the twelve winds <note>starting with the life-sustaining wind</note>. 

As stated in the Root Tantra:
The impure winds such as the life-sustaining wind,
Produced from the twelve links of the family,
Are explained as being within the houses <note>referring to the zodiac houses</note>.
The planets arise within those houses.
This wheel of twelve aspects
Is explained as the twelve links of existence.

<summary>This page describes the sixteen-fold classification of the Buddha's bodies and joys, leading to the "Stainless Light" state beyond dualities. It also introduces the correlation between the twelve links of dependent origination and the internal subtle winds.</summary>

ནི་ལྟེ་བ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནས་བརྩམས་ནས། ཆོས་དང་ལོངས་སྤྱོད་དག་པའོ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་མཐར། འཁོར་ལོ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་རྟེན་དང་བརྟེན་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་དང་། ལྟེ་བ་དང་ནི་མགྲིན་གསང་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནས་བརྩམས་ནས། རྡོ་རྗེ་དང་བཅས་རིས་དྲུག་གོ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་མཐར། རིགས་དྲུག་
གི་མཚན་ཉིད་དང་། དེ་རྣམས་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནས་བརྩམས་ནས། སྟེང་འོག་རྩ་གསུམ་ཉི་ཟླའི་མེ་དབྱེ་བས། གསུམ་རྣམས་ལ་གནས་པའོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་མཐར། རྩའི་དབྱེ་བས་རིགས་གསུམ་དང་། ལུས་ལ་དངོས་པོ་ཞུགས་ཏེ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནས་བརྩམས་ནས། ལུས་དང་དངོས་པོ་རབ་འབྱེད་
པའི། །ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་མཐར། ཁམས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་ལུས་དང་དངོས་པོའི་རང་བཞིན་དང་། ཤེས་རབ་ཐབས་ནི་རུས་པ་ཤ་སྟེ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནས་བརྩམས་ནས། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་དུ་ནི་རིག་པར་བྱ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་མཐར། ཐབས་དང་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕན་ཚུན་དུ་འཁྱུད་པའི་ཆོ་ག་དང་། རྩ་རྣམས་
སྟོང་ཕྲག་དྲུག་ནི་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནས་བརྩམས་ནས། ཟུང་གི་གྲངས་ནི་རིམ་པས་སོ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་མཐར། རྩ་རྣམས་འཕེལ་བ་དང་ཆད་པའི་མཚན་ཉིད་དང་། དཔལ་ལྡན་འབྱུང་བ་དབང་པོ་རྣམས། །ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནས་བརྩམས་ནས། བདག་ཉིད་ལས་ནི་ཟགས་པའོ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བའི་མཐར།

The stage is:
The second is Supreme Joy.
Then, through the power of union,
The fire of passion will blaze.
Because of that blazing, the <term>bindu</term> <gloss>vital essence</gloss> flows;
This is the third, the Pervasive Joy.
The <term>bindu</term> of body, speech, and mind
Appears at the final fourth stage.
Whatever the moment of self-knowing awareness is,
That is the fourth, the Co-emergent Joy.
By dividing those four through the <term>bindu</term> of body, speech,
Mind, and gnosis <note>original: "ye shes", referring to deep primordial wisdom</note>,
One should understand the reality
Of the sixteen-fold division.
Externally as well, that same reality,
Through the divisions of space and so forth,
Is the fifteen days of the lunar cycle and so on,
While the partless part is the sixteenth.
The first is freedom from passion; then great passion,
A blazing light of manifold colors.
The <term>Vajra</term> posture, the Perfect Buddha,
Who holds the perfect gathering of Buddhas.
Possessing all aspects, yet aspectless,
Holding the <term>bindu</term> divided into sixteen half-halves.
Partless and beyond calculation,
Holding the peak of the four concentrations <note>original: "bsam gtan", the four dhyanas or meditative absorptions</note>.
By the power of the gnosis of emptiness,
If it should happen in that way,
Then the four bodies of the Buddha
Will be attained without any doubt.
Having explained the meaning of those empowerments and so forth,
The master must certainly bestow them
Later upon the student
For the sake of the <term>ganachakra</term> <gloss>ritual feast circle</gloss>.
Once the student has received the manifest empowerment,
Then for one year, three years,
Six years, or twelve years,
They should listen to the Tantras and so forth.
The Root Tantra and the Condensed Tantra,
As well as the Explanatory Tantra,
Together with the commentaries and so forth,
Should be understood; then the Guru,
In order to purify the <term>Vajracharya</term> <gloss>Vajra Master</gloss>,
Should confer the Master's Empowerment.
Preceded by the signs of smoke and so forth,
The fourth empowerment should be given.
For the sake of the <term>Mahamudra</term> <gloss>Great Seal</gloss> accomplishment,
The six branches of yoga are explained.
Then, in a secluded place,
Together with the ten <term>mudras</term> <gloss>ritual seals or partners</gloss>,
The master should begin the activities.
Regarding that, the student should first
Take this vow at the feet of the Guru's lotus
Until the time of unsurpassable awakening:
From this time forward,
Until awakening <meta>continues to next page</meta>

<summary>This text describes the four joys of the tantric path and their relation to the sixteen-fold lunar divisions. It outlines the progression of a student from receiving initial empowerments to studying the Tantras and eventually receiving the fourth empowerment and practicing the six yogas.</summary>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>is emptiness endowed with the excellence of all aspects. <term>Gyü</term> <gloss>Cause</gloss> refers to the mind. Because it is characterized by being neither existent, nor non-existent, nor both, nor neither. Regarding the term <term>Drébu</term> <gloss>Fruit or Result</gloss>, it is the state of Buddhahood itself, the essence of compassion that is without any objective focus, which acts for the benefit of wandering beings. 

As it is said in the *Hevajra Tantra* of five hundred thousand verses:
The cause is first the emptiness,
Endowed with the excellence of all aspects;
Afterwards, through compassion without objective focus,
The fruit is acting for the benefit of wandering beings.

Therefore, the fruit of a cause that is not inherently established does not arise from a cause. Through phrases such as "the fruit," it is taught that if cause and fruit existed, there would be that which is to be sealed and a sealer. Since their inherent nature is not established, how could that be the case? 

If one asks, "Is it then the case that the entities of cause and fruit do not exist in any way whatsoever?" it is said here: regarding the term "cause" and so forth, the intention is that the entities of cause and fruit, which have the character of dependent origination, exist solely as conventional truth, established as true in the manner of an illusion and so forth. 

Therefore, it is the form of the union of the essence of <term>Prajna</term> <gloss>Wisdom</gloss> and <term>Upaya</term> <gloss>Method</gloss>, free from conceptualizing cause, fruit, and so forth, in which the primordial wisdom of great bliss arises at all times. This very point is taught by the sections beginning with "mutually" and so forth. 

As the venerable <term>Saraha</term> <gloss>an important Indian master and mahasiddha</gloss> said:
Always arising for beings, free from effort;
When it is definitely taught at that time,
Even the All-Knowing One becomes impoverished of words;
May the unique King of Bliss be victorious!

If, for the time being, phenomena are unproduced and unceasing, how then can they be established conventionally in the forms of the knowable and the knower?

<summary>This page discusses the tantric relationship between cause and fruit, defining them as emptiness and non-referential compassion respectively. It explains that while these lack inherent existence, they function as a union of wisdom and method within conventional reality.</summary>

དེ་ནས་ཞེས་པས་མཎྜལ་མེ་ཏོག་དང་བཅས་པ་ཕུལ་ཏེ་གསོལ་བ་བཏབ། ཡེ་ཤེས་དབབ་ཅིང་རྡོ་རྗེ་བཙུན་མོའི་ལུས་ལ་མེ་ཏོག་དོར། གདོང་ཕྱེ་བ་ནི་རྡོ་རྗེའི་སྤྱན་དབྱེ་བ་སྟེ། མ་རིག་པའི་མུན་པ་བསལ་བའོ། །ཡེ་ཤེས་ཀྱི་དོན་མཐོང་བར་བྱ་བ་ཆོས་ལ་ཆོས་ཀྱི་མིག་རྣམ་པར་དག་པ་ཆོས་
འབྱུང་གི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་བསྟན་པ་འབྱུང་བ་ལྔ་དག་པ་རྩའི་ཕོ་བྲང་ངོ་། །དཔལ་ཧེ་རུ་ཀའི་གནས་གང་ཡིན་ནི་རྡོ་རྗེ་ལུས་ཀྱི་གནས་དང་ཉེ་གནས་ལ་སོགས་པའོ། །དེར་ནི་ཡང་དག་པ་ངེས་པར་བསྟན་པར་བྱ། རྟེན་དང་བརྟེན་པར་བཅས་པའོ། །དེ་ནས་རྡོ་རྗེ་སློབ་དཔོན་གྱིས་རིག་མ་གཏད་ཅིང་
གདམས་པ་བསྟན་པས་སློབ་མ་དེ་རིག་མ་དང་མཉམ་གཞག་ཅེས་ལྷའི་ང་རྒྱལ་བརྟན་པ་མཁའ་གསང་བྱིན་གྱིས་བརླབས་བཞིན་པས། རབ་ཏུ་འདུད་པ་བྱས་ནས་ནི། །ཞེས་རྩ་དབུ་མའི་སྣ་རྩེ་འཕྲོད་པས་ཟག་བཅས་རླུང་འགོག་པའོ། །གཡོན་ནས་བརྩམས་པའི་རིམ་པ་ནི་རྡོ་རྗེ་དབྱིངས་ཀྱི་
དབང་ཕྱུག་མའི་རྩ་བཙལ་བ་ལས་དགའ་བ་དང་སྐད་ཅིག་མ་རྟོགས་པར་བྱའོ། །དེར་ནི་བསྐོར་བ་རབ་ཏུ་བྱ་བས་ཏེ། སྙོམས་པར་འཇུག་པས་བསྲུང་བའི་སྦྱོར་བའོ། །དེ་ལ་ནི། དྲིལ་སྦྱངས་མེ་ཏོག་སྤོས་ཀྱིས་བརྒྱན། །ཤིན་ཏུ་སྒྲ་སྙན་དྲིལ་བུ་འཁྲོལ། །བསྒྲུབ་པ་པོ་ཡིས་རྔ་བརྡུང་ཞིང་། །དཀྱིལ་
འཁོར་དང་ནི་བླ་མ་ལ། །ཧ་ཧ་ཞེས་ནི་བརྗོད་པར་བྱ་བའི་དོན་ལ། དེས་ལྷན་ཅིག་སྐྱེས་པའི་ཡེ་ཤེས་བདེ་བ་ཆེན་པོ་སྔོན་དུ་བྱ་བའོ། །དེས་ནི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་འཁོར་ལོའི་ལམ་ལས་དོན་གྱིས་ཡེ་ཤེས་གསང་བ་བླ་ན་མེད་པ་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་གྱི་ནུབ་ཕྱོགས་སུ་ནི། དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་དང་ནི་བླ་མ་ལ། །ཇི་བཞིན་
ཆོ་གས་ཕྱག་བྱའོ། །ཞེས་དེ་ཉིད་མཆོད་ཅིང་མཉེས་པར་བྱའོ། །ད་ནི་དབང་བཞིའི་གདམས་པ་ཅུང་ཟད་བསྟན་པ་ནི། དཔལ་པདྨ་བཛྲ་པའི་བཞེད་པས། །དབང་གི་རྣམ་བཞི་ངེས་པ་ལས། །ཡོན་ཏན་བཞིར་གྱུར་ནུས་པར་ལྡན། །བསྐལ་པ་ལ་དབང་དྲི་མ་འཁྲུ། །རིགས་དེས་བསྟན་པར་གྱུར་པ་ལ། །

Now, the third empowerment will be explained. 

The phrase "then" refers to offering a <term>mandala</term> <gloss>sacred cosmogram</gloss> together with flowers and making a formal request. The wisdom is descended, and flowers are cast upon the body of the <term>Vajra Consort</term>. The "opening of the face" refers to the opening of the <term>Vajra eye</term>, which clears away the darkness of ignorance. To see the meaning of wisdom, the pure eye of reality <note>original: "dharma"</note> is shown as the <term>dharmodaya</term> <gloss>source of reality</gloss> mandala, which is the palace of the channels where the five elements are purified. 

The phrase "whatever the abode of glorious Heruka is" refers to the places and secondary places within the <term>Vajra body</term> <note>the subtle energy body</note>. There, the truth shall be perfectly and decisively shown. This includes both the support <note>the environment or palace</note> and the supported <note>the deities or inhabitants</note>. 

Then, the <term>Vajra Master</term> hands over the <term>vidya</term> <gloss>consort or wisdom woman</gloss> and provides the instructions. The student enters into meditative equipoise with the <term>vidya</term>. While maintaining the firm pride of the deity and blessing the <term>secret space</term> <gloss>the sexual organ</gloss>, the text says: "Having performed the great bowing." This refers to blocking the contaminated winds by joining the tips of the central channel <note>the union of the central channels of the practitioners</note>. 

The sequence beginning from the left involves seeking the channel of <term>Vajradhatvishvari</term> <gloss>Lady Sovereign of the Vajra Realm</gloss>, through which joy and the "instantaneous moment" are to be realized. In that state, "circumambulation should be performed," which refers to the application of protection through meditative union. Regarding that: "Adorned with cleaned grains, flowers, and incense; sounding the bell with a very sweet melody; the practitioner beats the drum; and to the mandala and the Guru, one should utter 'Ha Ha'." 

The meaning of this is to bring the <term>sahaja-jnana</term> <gloss>innate co-emergent wisdom</gloss> of great bliss to the forefront. By means of that path of the mandala cycle, the supreme secret wisdom is realized. In the western direction of the mandala, "one should prostrate to the mandala and the Guru according to the ritual." In this way, one should worship and please that very reality.

Now, a brief teaching on the instructions of the four empowerments is presented according to the view of the glorious <term>Padmavajra</term>: "From the certainty of the four types of empowerment, one possesses the capacity for the four qualities. One gains power over the eons and washes away stains. Through that lineage, it is revealed..."

<summary>This page details the ritual procedures for the third empowerment, focusing on the union of the practitioner and consort to realize innate wisdom and great bliss. It describes the symbolic opening of the eye of wisdom and the purification of the subtle body channels.</summary>
<keywords>third empowerment, Heruka, Vajra body, sahaja-jnana, Padmavajra, mandala, bodhicitta, consort ritual</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the secret paths of the Vidyadhara (Knowledge-Holders) within the Tantric tradition, specifically focusing on the characteristics of the consort and the yogic practices of the body.</meta>

...becomes <note>referring to a spiritual transformation or realization</note>. Furthermore, that individual, through specifically what is described, comes to understand the meaning of remaining on the secret path of the <term>Rigden</term> <gloss>Kalki or Lineage Holder</gloss>. Having shown this in brief, now follows the detailed explanation. 

Regarding the teaching on the objects of enjoyment for the <term>yogi</term> <gloss>practitioner</gloss>: the "brother" <note>likely referring to a spiritual peer or a specific male energy</note> is motivated by intense passion. Alternatively, the "father" is viewed in terms of the producer and the produced; the "Lord" who has become close is viewed through simultaneous observation as being inseparable. By seeing the wisdom in that very moment of the gathering <note>the assembly of deities or energies</note>, one is oriented toward the arising of qualities by seeing wisdom in the moment of union.

Here, in order to specifically show the classes of <term>Rigma</term> <gloss>spiritual consort or Vidyā</gloss> of the <term>Vajra</term> <gloss>Indestructible</gloss> family, the physical distinctions are described: 

The tongue is thick, meaning the tongue is rounded and long. The eyes are yellowish-red, appearing like those of an owl, wide and long-shaped. The hair is coarse and black. All the body hairs are yellowish-red and stand upward or are curled. She is endowed with spiritual qualities. 

Regarding <term>Siddhi</term> <gloss>spiritual accomplishments</gloss>, she manifests the supreme attainment. As for the common accomplishments, these are:
*   The sword <note>power over the sword</note>
*   The <term>Vetala</term> <gloss>zombie or animated corpse</gloss>
*   The magic vase
*   Swift-footedness <note>miraculous speed</note>
*   Alchemy <note>turning base metals to gold</note>
*   The elixir of longevity
*   Invisibility
*   Walking in the sky

These are all accomplished through the power of the practice. The common accomplishments are born of the <term>Mantra</term> <gloss>sacred sound</gloss>. 

The "conduct" <note>the yogic vow</note> consists of abiding in the supreme pride <note>divine identity</note>, utilizing the four <term>Nyingpo</term> <gloss>Essence Mantras</gloss> and <term>Nye-nying</term> <gloss>Heart Mantras</gloss> and so forth. Finding joy in these means that after receiving empowerment, one constantly keeps them in mind. 

"Equipped with mindfulness" means the application of mindfulness to the body, specifically viewing one's own body as the form of the deity. Regarding "feeling," one abides in bliss. Regarding "phenomena," one remains in the state of wisdom because bliss is sealed by emptiness. Regarding "mind," it is the mindfulness of the ultimate meaning, abiding in non-duality, self-liberation, non-arising, and the absence of conceptual elaboration. 

The <term>messenger</term> <gloss>dakini</gloss> and others include the "innately born," "field-born," and "mantra-born" <note>three classifications of dakinis</note>. Alternatively, they refer to the seven classes of <term>Yoginis</term>. 

"Together with the places" refers to the external places: the subterranean, the terrestrial, and the celestial. Internally, these refer to the twenty-four places of the body and so forth, where they dwell together with the <term>Dakas</term> <gloss>heroes</gloss>. There, the yogi relies on the <term>Vajra</term> body and binds the vital points. By forcefully constraining the winds <note>the subtle breaths</note>, one strikes the vital points of the channels <note>nadis</note>, such as the syllables <term>Pu</term>, <term>Ja</term>, <term>O</term>, <term>A</term>, and so forth. When the wind and mind merge into one, all the <term>Dakinis</term> of the body's vital channels appear in the form of syllables...

<summary>This page details the physical characteristics of a Vajra-family consort and lists common siddhis like invisibility and alchemy. It also explains the internal yogic practice of binding subtle winds and syllables within the body's channels to achieve non-dual wisdom.</summary>
<keywords>Siddhi, Dakini, Vajra Body, Subtle Winds, Yoga, Consort, Mantra, Mindfulness</keywords>

It is said, "All phenomena are purified by mantra." When generating the eight meditative concentrations, the eleventh mantra is the purification of the wrathful ones; it is said, "All phenomena are purified by the wrathful ones." When generating the Wheel of the Mind <note>the central portion of the mandala associated with the enlightened mind</note>, the twelfth mantra is the purification of the mind; it is said, "All phenomena are purified by the mind." When generating the Wheel of Speech, the thirteenth mantra is purification; it is said, "All phenomena are purified by the pure." When generating the Wheel of the Body, the fourteenth mantra is the purification of the body; "All phenomena are purified by the body." When causing the <term>jnanasattva</term> <gloss>wisdom being</gloss> to enter, the fifteenth mantra is the purification of the nectar of wisdom; "All phenomena are purified by the nectar of wisdom."

When donning the armor of the heroes and heroines <note>a ritual visualization where deities protect the practitioner's body parts</note>, the sixteenth mantra is the purification of various <term>samaya</term> <gloss>sacred commitments</gloss>; "All phenomena are purified by various commitments." When performing the recitation <note>mantra recitation</note>, the seventeenth mantra is the purification of conduct; "All phenomena are purified by conduct." When meditating on the <term>samayasattva</term> <gloss>commitment being</gloss> with the <term>jnanasattva</term> <gloss>wisdom being</gloss> at its heart, and the <term>samadhisattva</term> <gloss>concentration being</gloss> as a hand-symbol or seed-syllable at that heart, the eighteenth mantra is the purification of the three yogas; "All phenomena are purified by the three yogas."

When bestowing the empowerment, the nineteenth mantra is the purification of empowerment; "All phenomena are purified by empowerment." When radiating the eight goddesses through the mantra of eight lines, the twentieth mantra is the purification of offerings; "All phenomena are purified by offerings." When meditating on the four joys of the father and mother <note>the union of the male and female deities</note>, the twenty-first mantra is "I am the nature of the non-dual offering of all the <term>Tathagatas</term> <gloss>Buddhas</gloss>." When meditating on the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the twenty-second mantra is the purification of the mandala; "The mandala of all phenomena is purified." When meditating on the central father and mother alone, the twenty-third mantra is the purification of the lord; "All phenomena are purified by the lord." When meditating on the twenty-four elements as heroes, the twenty-fourth mantra is the purification of the heroes; "All phenomena are purified by the heroes." When meditating on the twenty-four as heroines…

<summary>This text details a sequence of twenty-four mantras used during Tantric visualization practices to purify different aspects of reality and the meditative process. It links specific ritual stages, such as the generation of the three wheels and the donning of deity armor, to the concept of universal purity.</summary>
<keywords>mantra, purification, mandala, jnanasattva, samaya, three yogas, empowerment, four joys, thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, heroes and heroines</keywords>

གཞན་དང་གཞན་གྱིས་གཟུགས་སུ་བསྒོམ་པའི་ཚེ། རྒྱུད་སྡེ་བཞིའི་ལྷ་ཐ་དད་པའི་རྗེས་སུ་འབྲང་ཡང་། ལྷ་དེའི་སྙིང་གར་ནམ་མཁའ་ལྡིང་གི་གདོང་ཅན་གྱི་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་བསྒོམས་ན། ཆར་འབབ་པར་འགྱུར་རོ། །འདིས་ནི་འདི་སྐད་སྟོན་པ་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེའི་སྙིང་གར་ཕྱིར་བཟློག་ཆེན་མོ་
ལ་སོགས་པ་ལས་བརྒྱ་བྱེད་པའི་དུས་ལྷའི་སྙིང་གར་བསྒོམས་ནས་ལས་བརྒྱ་བྱེད་དོ་ཞེས་བསྡུས་པ་ལས་ཀྱང་གསུངས་སོ། །གལ་ཏེ་སྙིང་གར་མི་བསྒོམ་ན་ཕྱག་མཚན་གྱི་དབུས་སུ་བསྒོམས་ནས་ཀྱང་ལས་ཚོགས་བྱེད་པ་ནི། མདུང་རྩེ་གསུམ་པ་ལ་ནམ་མཁའ་ལྡིང་གི་གདོང་ཅན་གྱི་
འཁོར་ལོ་བྲིས་ན་སེར་བ་གཅོད་པ་ཅང་ཏེའུ་ལ་བྲིས་ནས་མེ་རེངས་པར་བྱེད་ཅེས་བྱ་བ་ནས་གླང་པོ་ཆེའི་པགས་པ་ལ་བྲིས་ན། དཔག་ཚད་སྟོང་ཕྲག་བརྒྱར་འགྲོ་འོང་བྱེད་དོ། །སྙིང་གར་མི་བསྒོམ་ན་ཕྱག་རྒྱ་དྲུག་ལས་འཁོར་ལོ་བྲིས་ན་མི་སྣང་བ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་ལས་དྲུག་བྱེད་པར་
འགྱུར་རོ། །ལེའུ་སུམ་ཅུ་རྩ་བཞིའི་འགྲེལ་པའོ།། །།དེ་ལྟར་ཀླུ་འདུལ་བའི་དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་བཤད་ནས། དེ་ནས་གཞན་ཡང་བཤད་བྱ་བ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བས་ཕུར་བུའི་ལྷ་སྟོན་ཏོ། །རྒྱུད་སྡེ་བཞི་ལས་ཕུར་བུའི་སྲུང་བ་སྣ་ཚོགས་བཤད་པ། གསང་བ་མཆོག་གི་རྒྱུད་འདིར་མདོར་
བསྡུས་ན་གསུངས་པ་ནི། ཕུར་བུ་བསྒོམ་པར་འདོད་པས་སྔོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བ་ལྔ་དང་འབྱུང་བཞི་རི་རབ་སྣ་ཚོགས་རྡོ་རྗེ་དང་གཞལ་ཡས་ཁང་བསྐྱེད་ལ། པདྨའི་ལྟེ་བར་ཡི་གེ་ཧཱུཾ་ལས་སྐད་ཅིག་གིས་རྫུས་སྐྱེས་ཀྱི་ཧེ་རུ་ཀ་ཞབས་གཅིག་པ་བསྒོམ་པ་ནི་དང་པོ་སྦྱོར་བའོ། །སྐུ་མདོག་
སྔོན་པོ་ཞལ་དྲུག་པ་ཕྱག་བཅུ་གཉིས་པ་ཞབས་གཅིག་པ་ཡུམ་རྡོ་རྗེ་ཕག་མོ་ཞབས་གཅིག་པར་བསྒོམས་ཏེ་གོ་སླའོ། །འཁོར་བཤད་པ་ནི། ཤར་ལྷོ་མཚམས་སུ་གཤིན་རྗེ་བརྟན་མ་གླང་པོ་ཆེའི་གདོང་ཅན་ཞབས་གཅིག་པ། ནུབ་བྱང་མཚམས་སུ་གཤིན་རྗེ་མཆེ་བ་

Perform the ritual bath. If you create a nine-headed image made from the mud of both riverbanks and perform the <term>abhiseka</term> <gloss>water empowerment</gloss> upon it, rain will fall. Having explained the ritual applications, I will now explain the general ritual. When performing the hundred activities of the <term>karmatshog</term> <gloss>collection of rites</gloss>, even if one follows the various deities of the four classes of <term>tantra</term> and meditates on their various forms, if one meditates on the Garuda-faced <term>Heruka</term> <gloss>blood-drinker deity</gloss> at the heart of that deity, rain will fall. This indicates that during the hundred activities such as the Great Reversal <note>original: "phyir bzlog chen mo", a rite to repel negativity</note>, one should meditate on this at the deity’s heart to accomplish the hundred tasks, as stated in the Summary.

If one does not meditate on it at the heart, one may also perform the activities by meditating on it in the center of the hand-symbols. If the <term>cakra</term> <gloss>wheel or diagram</gloss> of the Garuda-faced one is drawn on a triple-pointed spear, it stops hail. If drawn on a <term>damaru</term> <gloss>hand-drum</gloss>, it causes fire to be transfixed. If drawn on elephant skin, one can travel back and forth over a hundred thousand <term>yojana</term> <gloss>a distance of roughly 4 to 9 miles</gloss>. If one does not meditate at the heart but draws the wheel on the six <term>mudra</term> <gloss>ritual ornaments or gestures</gloss>, the six activities such as invisibility will be accomplished. This concludes the commentary on the thirty-fourth chapter.

Having explained the <term>mandala</term> for subduing the <term>naga</term> <gloss>serpent spirits</gloss>, the text says, Next, another shall be explained, which reveals the deity of the <term>kila</term> <gloss>ritual dagger</gloss>. Regarding the various protections of the ritual dagger explained in the four classes of tantra, they are summarized in this Supreme Secret Tantra as follows. One who wishes to meditate on the ritual dagger should first generate the five preliminaries, the four elements, Mount Meru, the crossed <term>vajra</term>, and the celestial palace. Then, at the hub of a lotus, from the syllable <term>HUM</term>, one instantaneously meditates on the single-legged Heruka born through transformation; this is the initial application. He is blue in color with six faces, twelve arms, and one leg, meditating on him with the consort Vajravarahi <note>the Diamond Sow</note>, who also has one leg; this is easy to understand. Regarding the retinue: in the Southeast is Yamadanti with an elephant face and one leg. In the Northwest is Yamadhadi…

<summary>This page describes ritual instructions for weather control and travel using the Garuda-faced Heruka, followed by the visualization of a single-legged Heruka deity and consort for ritual dagger practices.</summary>
<keywords>Heruka, Garuda, weather magic, cakra, ritual dagger, kila, Vajravarahi, naga subduing</keywords>

འཛིན་ཅིང་མ་ཧེ་ལ་ཁྲོས་པའི་ཚུལ་གྱིས་བཞུགས་པ་བྲིའོ། །ཆུ་བདག་ནི་སྐུ་མདོག་དཀར་པོ་གདེངས་ཀ་བདུན་དང་ལྡན་པ། སྦྲུལ་གྱི་ཞགས་པ་དང་དུང་འཛིན་པ་ཆུ་སྲིན་ལ་བཞུགས་པའོ། །ནོར་བདག་ནི་སྐུ་མདོག་སེར་པོ་གསེར་གྱི་མདོག་ཅན་རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་དབུ་རྒྱན་
ཅན་ལྕགས་ཀྱུ་དང་དབྱུག་པ་འཛིན་པ་གནོད་སྦྱིན་ལ་བཞུགས་པའོ། །དབང་ལྡན་ནི་སྐུ་མདོག་དཀར་པོ་རལ་པའི་ཐོར་ཚུགས་ཅན་ཟླ་བའི་དབུ་རྒྱན། སྤྱན་གསུམ་པ་ཐོད་པའི་ཕྲེང་བ་ཅན། ཕྱག་བཞི་པ། ཅང་ཏེའུ་དང་། ཐོད་པ་དང་། ཏྲི་ཤཱུ་ལ། ཁ་ཊྭཱཾ་ག་འཛིན་པ་ཁྱུ་མཆོག་གི་སྟེང་དུ་
བཞུགས་པའོ། །མེ་ལྷ་ནི་སྐུ་མདོག་དམར་པོ་རལ་པ་ཐོར་ཚུགས་སུ་བྱས་པ། ཚངས་པའི་ཐེ་གུ་ཅན། ཕྱག་བཞི་པ། བགྲང་ཕྲེང་དང་སྐྱབས་སྦྱིན་དང་གུནྡྷེ་དང་། དབྱུག་པ་འཛིན་པ་རའི་སྟེང་ན་བཞུགས་པའོ། །བདེན་བྲལ་ནི་སྐུ་མདོག་སྔོན་པོ་དབུ་སྐྲ་དམར་པོ་གྱེན་དུ་འབར་བ།
ཐོད་པའི་ཕྲེང་བ་ཅན་གྲི་གུག་དང་ཐོད་པ་འཛིན་པ་རོའི་སྟེང་ན་བཞུགས་པའོ། །རླུང་ནི་དུ་བའི་མདོག་ཅན་རླུང་གི་རས་འཛིན་པ། རིན་པོ་ཆེའི་དབུ་རྒྱན་ཅན་ཤ་བའི་སྟེང་ན་བཞུགས་པ་བྲིའོ། །དེ་དག་གི་གནས་སུ་ཡང་ལྷ་དང་{ཡི་དགས་,ཡི་དྭགས་}དང་ཀླུ་དང་གནོད་སྦྱིན་དང་འབྱུང་པོ་དང་ཐུབ་པ་དང་།

The male and female deer <note>original: "ri dags"</note> represent those who follow through faith and the study of the teachings <note>original: "dharma"</note>, thus purifying the application to the path. Regarding the Wheel of Dharma <note>original: "dharmacakra"</note>, the male and female deer with fearful necks represent the purification of the application to that Wheel. The purification of moral shame <note>original: "hrī"</note> is represented by canopies, garments, garlands, and the like.

Because there is no separate binding from any side, the Vajra Garland represents the purification of the turning of the Wheel of Dharma in the manner of the Vajra of all Perfectly Awakened Buddhas. The blazing rays of light represent the purification of the vision of primordial wisdom. The colors of the ground and so forth represent the purification of Vairochana and the other <note>Dhyani Buddhas</note>. Other elements are not written here because they are already well known. 

In this way, having visualized the tiered mansion <note>original: "kūṭāgāra"</note>, one should visualize oneself as the Bhagavan <gloss>Blessed Lord</gloss> in its center upon a multi-colored lotus and the other seats in the previous order. The three syllables *Om Ah Hum*, which are the nature of Body, Speech, and Mind, are enclosed between two red *Ho* syllables. This is known as the being of the intermediate state <term>bardo</term>. With great joy, it enters through the mouth of the Bhagavan, passes through the path of the Vajra <note>the secret organ</note>, and enters the lotus <note>the womb</note> of the consort, where it melts in the stomach. The Bhagavan also, through ultimate great passion, melts together with his own consort <term>rig ma</term>. He remains in the nature of Great Bliss in the form of the Mind of Awakening <term>bodhichitta</term>, which is like liquid mercury.

Then, without interruption, the yoginis such as Pukkasi, who are the nature of Great Loving-kindness and the other <note>Four Immeasurables</note>, feel great distress in their minds, thinking, "We are without a protector!" They cry out:

"Venerable One, let your mind of compassion arise!
Pukkasi, protect me!
Abandon the state of sheer emptiness,
And grant me the union of Great Bliss.
If you are absent, I will perish,
O Hevajra, please arise!
Abandon the state of sheer emptiness,
And grant the fruition of Shavari <note>the mountain goddess</note>.
O Lord of Joy, who cares for the guests of the world,
Have you entered into Emptiness?
Without you, the directions are unknown..."

<summary>This page describes the symbolic correspondences of the mandala and details a generation stage visualization involving the melting of the deity into liquid bodhichitta. It includes a liturgical petition from the yoginis to the deity Hevajra to arise from the state of emptiness for the sake of beings.</summary>
<keywords>Hevajra, generation stage, bodhichitta, yoginis, Pukkasi, Great Bliss, Emptiness, mandala symbolism, bardo</keywords>

ཀྱིས་ང་ལ་གསོལ་བཏབ་པ། །སྐུ་གཟུགས་དག་ནི་ཁྱད་པར་དུ། །ཇི་སྐད་གསུངས་བཞིན་རབ་གནས་པ། །དེ་ནི་ངས་བྱས་བྱེད་དུ་བཅུག །ཁྱེད་ཀྱིས་དེ་ནི་ཀུན་རྫོགས་པར། །ཅི་བདེ་བར་ནི་མཆོད་པར་གྱིས། །དེ་ནས་སྲུང་མ་བསྒོ་བ་ནི། །བདག་ཉིད་ལྷག་པའི་ལྷར་སྦྱོར་བས། །ནག་
པོ་ཆེན་པོ་དགུག་པ་དང་། །གཞུག་དང་བཅིང་དང་དབང་དུ་བྱ། །དེ་ལ་མཆོད་དང་གཏོར་མ་སྦྱིན། །དེ་ལ་བཀའ་ལུང་བསྒོ་བྱ་བ། །ང་ཡིས་རབ་གནས་བྱས་པ་ཡི། །གཙུག་ལག་ཁང་ལ་སོགས་པ་འདི། །ཇི་སྲིད་གནས་པ་དེ་སྲིད་དུ། །བསྲུང་ཞིང་ཁྱོད་ཀྱིས་ལེགས་པར་སྐྱོངས། །
དཀོན་མཆོག་འཕགས་པའི་དགེ་འདུན་གྱི། །བཀའ་སྩལ་ཁྱོད་ཀྱིས་བསྲུང་བ་དང་། །སྟོན་པའི་བཀའ་དང་སློབ་དཔོན་གྱི། །བཀའ་ལུང་བསྒོ་བ་ལེགས་པར་སྲུངས། །དེ་ནས་བཟོད་གསོལ་བྱ་སྟེ། རྫོགས་སངས་རྒྱས་དང་ལྷ་རྣམས་དང་། །དེ་སྲས་ཚངས་སོགས་ལྷ་ཚོགས་ཀུན། །
གང་ཞིག་ཆོ་ག་བྱས་པ་ནི། །ནོངས་གྱུར་དེ་དག་བཟོད་མཛད་རིགས། །དེ་ནས་གཤེགས་གསོལ་བྱེད་འདོད་ན། །འདི་ཙམ་བརྗོད་པར་བྱ་བ་སྟེ། །སྦྱིན་བདག་རྣམས་ལ་ཞི་བ་དང་། །བདེ་ལེགས་ཆེན་པོ་ཀུན་མཛད་པར། །སངས་རྒྱས་ཡུལ་དུ་གཤེགས་ནས་ཀྱང་། །སླར་ཡང་

Similarly, this applies to the canopies and other ornaments. Again, after performing the ritual bath, one should present the five types of offerings. Then, the food offerings are presented. Following this, the words of offering should be applied as before, while reciting: May all sentient beings be liberated from the eons of hunger, thirst, and famine. <term>Om sarva tathagata ahara bhrum ja shri samaye hum</term> <gloss>Om, O all Thus-gone Ones, take this food, may the auspicious commitment be established, hum.</gloss>

Then, the robes are offered with the prayer: May all sentient beings be free from the sufferings of lacking clothes and garments, and may they possess the fortune of wearing the divine <term>panchalika</term> <gloss>fine silken cloth</gloss> garments, which bring bliss when touched. <term>Om sarva tathagata vastra nana shri samaye hum</term> <gloss>Om, O all Thus-gone Ones, may these various auspicious clothes establish the commitment, hum.</gloss>

Next, the warming of the presence should be performed. This is done through the fire offering. It is conducted both for the purpose of bringing auspiciousness to the disciples and for the sake of satisfying the deities. This is done according to the previous ritual procedures. Then, as a special measure, offerings for the inner physical forms and a feast of <term>charu</term> <gloss>sacrificial cooked grain or pap</gloss> should also be prepared.

Following that, the entrustment to the object of worship is performed: You have made a request to me regarding these specific physical forms. I have performed the consecration, or caused it to be performed, exactly as described in the scriptures. Now that the ritual is fully complete, you may worship them as you wish in happiness.

Then, the command to the protector is given. By uniting oneself with the supreme deity <note>referring to the practitioner assuming the identity of the yidam</note>, one should summon, enter, bind, and bring under one's power the Great Black One <note>Mahakala</note>. Offerings and sacrificial cakes <gloss>tormas</gloss> are given to him. Then the command should be pronounced: This temple and its contents, which I have consecrated, must be guarded and well-protected by you for as long as they remain. You must guard the commands of the Noble Community of the Triple Gem. Properly guard the commands of the Teacher and the instructions of the Master.

Then, the request for forgiveness is made: The Perfect Buddhas, the deities, their sons, and the hosts of gods such as Brahma; whatever errors were made in the performance of this ritual, it is right that you forgive them.

Then, if one wishes to perform the request to depart, these words should be spoken: Having brought peace and great well-being to the patrons, please depart for the Buddha-realms, and then return again...

<summary>This page describes the final stages of a consecration ritual, including the offering of food and robes, the command to Mahakala to protect the temple, and a prayer for forgiveness for ritual errors.</summary>

ཡོན་ཏན་གཏེར་ནི་གྲགས་པའོ། །སྣ་ཚོགས་པདྨ་འདབ་བརྒྱད་པའི། །རྒྱལ་བ་མཆོག་གི་པད་གནས་སུ། །སྙིང་གའི་ནམ་མཁའི་དབུས་སུ་ནི། །འོད་ཟེར་གཟུགས་ཅན་ཕྱག་རྒྱར་གྲགས། །རོ་དྲུག་ཉམས་སུ་མྱོང་བ་ཡི། །གནས་སུ་དགྱེས་པའི་མཐའ་ཅན་ཡིན། །བཅུ་གཉིས་ཕྱེད་ཀྱི་
ཕྱེད་འོད་ཟེར། །རང་བཞིན་གྱིས་ནི་དཔེ་མེད་གྲགས། །གང་དུ་སྐུ་གསུམ་རྣམ་པར་གཤེགས། །ཐོད་པའི་མཚམས་ནི་གསང་བ་ཡི། །པདྨ་ཡི་ནི་སྙིང་པོའི་ཚིགས། །རྒྱས་པའི་བུ་ག་གསང་བ་ཡི། །དྲི་མ་མེད་པ་ནམ་མཁའི་དབུས། །མཚན་མའི་བདག་པོ་ཀུན་དུ་གང་། །མུན་གནག་ཡར་

བསྟན་པ། །རྒྱལ་བ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས་རྙེད་པ་དཀའ། །དེ་ནི་རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དག་སྐུ། །མཆོག་གི་དབང་ཕྱུག་རྒྱལ་གྱུར་ཅིག །ཡོན་ཏན་ལྡན་པའི་བླ་ཞལ་ནས། །གང་གིས་དེ་ཡི་སྒྲ་ཉན་པ། །མཆོག་གི་དམ་པ་དགེ་བ་ཅན། །དེ་ནི་སྐྱེས་བུས་བལྟ་བཀུར་འོས། །སྣ་ཚོགས་དུ་མར་རྣམ་པར་

In the center of the heart of <term>Vajrasattva</term> <gloss>the Adamantine Being</gloss> is the <term>bindu</term> <gloss>drop or point of essence</gloss> known as the formless body. Sixty plus six <note>original: "drug gis lhag pa'i drug bcu", likely referring to sixty-six</note> petals are reduced by two at the navel; it is marked by the supreme bliss of the moon.

The treasure of qualities is famous. In the supreme lotus-abode of the <term>Jina</term> <gloss>Conqueror or Buddha</gloss>, which has eight petals of various kinds, in the center of the space of the heart, is known as the radiant mudra of form. In the place where the six tastes are experienced, it ends in joy. Half of half of twelve <note>three</note> are the rays of light. By its very nature, it is known as incomparable.

Where the three bodies <note>original: "sku gsum", referring to the Dharmakaya, Sambhogakaya, and Nirmanakaya</note> depart, at the junction of the skull is the secret joint of the essence of the lotus. In the center of the stainless space of the secret opening of expansion, the lord of signs is completely full. With the waxing of the dark moon, the rising of liberation from the clouds of conceptual thought occurs. Although it expands in the center of the heart, it cannot be expressed in speech. If one were to express it through words, one would be describing something other than the actual meaning. Because it is experienced by oneself, it is superior by its nature alone.

The one who has shown such a path is difficult even for the <term>Jinas</term> <gloss>Conquerors</gloss> to find. That is the body of <term>Vajrasattva</term>; may the supreme lord be victorious! Whoever hears that sound from the mouth of a qualified guru is a supreme, virtuous, and holy person. Such a person is worthy of being seen and honored by men.

One who has abandoned various mental constructions and possesses a one-pointed mind, drawing near in an uninterrupted stream, enters the yoga of meditative concentration <note>term: "bsam gtan", original: dhyana</note>. Free from the dark clouds of <term>samsara</term> <gloss>the cycle of existence</gloss>, such a person is worthy of being touched and honored by men. A jewel distinguished by six qualities, difficult even for the sons of the Buddha to find, which opens the intellect of those with firm wisdom—whoever is deeply absorbed in meditation upon it, free from the conceptualizations of liberation, that person is worthy of being worshiped and honored by men. To the Mother <note>This refers to the primary female deity or the essence of wisdom</note>, with the meditation of <term>Om yatha sarva tathagata stas tatha aham</term> <gloss>Om, as are all the Tathagatas, so am I</gloss>, one proceeds just as the previous Buddhas have proceeded. Because one has thus gone and awakened, they are called a <term>Tathagata</term> <gloss>Thus-Gone One</gloss>. Because they have conquered the four <term>maras</term> <gloss>demonic obstructions to enlightenment</gloss>, they are an <term>Arhat</term> <gloss>Foe-Destroyer</gloss>. For that very reason, because they have perfectly and unmistakably realized and awakened to all things, it is said they have become a <term>Samyaksambuddha</term> <gloss>Perfectly Complete Buddha</gloss>; this refers to "perfection."

This demonstrates that the essence of all Buddhas is gathered into one within the nature of <term>Vairocana</term> <gloss>The Illuminator</gloss>. To show how blessings and empowerments are bestowed according to the needs of those to be tamed, the text says "Then..." and so forth. The phrase "from that Vajrasattva of all the Tathagatas" means from the one residing in the heart of Vairocana.

The jewel empowerment of <term>Akashagarbha</term> <gloss>Essence of Space</gloss> is the bestowing of the crown empowerment of the <term>Vajraratna</term> <gloss>Adamantine Jewel</gloss> through the mantra <term>Vajra Ratna</term>. Regarding the statement "generate the Dharma-wisdom of the Lord who views all," <term>Avalokiteshvara</term> <gloss>The Lord Who Looks Down with Compassion</gloss> has already been explained. His "Dharma" refers to the previously described teachings of Vairocana and Great Vairocana, and the domain of the emanated mandala such as <term>Vajrasattva</term> <gloss>Vajra Being</gloss>. His "wisdom" is the realization, and that is what is generated.

This indicates that after the empowerment, the five types of permission <note>ritual authorizations</note> mentioned in the phrase "throughout all worlds" and so forth are given for the sake of entering the mandala and turning the wheel of Dharma. The phrase "having established them in all the activities of all the Tathagatas" refers to performing the benefit of beings through the ritual of drawing the mandala. These are all the activities of all the Tathagatas. Having bestowed the empowerment and the permission, one enters into the work of drawing the mandala.

<summary>This page explains the titles of a Buddha and describes the process of receiving empowerments and permissions from Vairocana to perform mandala rituals for the benefit of beings.</summary>
<keywords>Tathagata, Vairocana, empowerment, mandala, Akashagarbha, Avalokiteshvara, Vajraratna, ritual activity</keywords>

One should liberate <note>The context suggests the liberation of sentient beings or the dissolution of concepts</note> in that manner. After completing the <term>Mahayoga</term> <gloss>Great Yoga</gloss> in this way, one should bind the <term>mudra</term> <gloss>ritual hand gesture</gloss> of the <term>Bhagavan Vajrahumkara</term> <gloss>The Victorious One Who Makes the Sound Hum</gloss>. With the mind, one dwells in the direction of the sky. On a <term>mandala</term> <gloss>circular disk</gloss> of wind, one should meditate on a blazing <term>vajra</term> <gloss>ritual scepter</gloss> arising from the syllable <term>Hum</term>. At the center of the vajra, one should meditate on the syllable <term>Ba</term>. 

Then, from that vajra, a turbulent mass of blazing vajra light rays emerges. One should imagine that these rays, like the great fire at the end of an eon, reduce all buddhafields to ashes. Then, in the direction of the sky, one should meditate on the syllable <term>Kham</term>, which is equal in size to the three thousandfold world system. It is the nature of <term>Vairocana</term> <gloss>The Illuminator</gloss>, white in color, and holds a stream of nectar. It washes the burned buddhafields. After washing them, one should imagine all those empty buddhafields as a great ocean of nectar, possessing garlands of turbulent waves, similar to an ocean of milk. 

Then, having placed the syllable <term>Ram</term> upon that great ocean, the fire of the syllable <term>Ram</term> boils the great ocean. From the remaining syllable <term>Pam</term>, one should imagine a great lotus surrounded by immeasurable small lotuses. Furthermore, at the root of that lotus, one should meditate on a gold-colored syllable <term>Pra</term>. Imagine an immeasurable golden turtle as the foundation for all the lotuses. 

Furthermore, at the center of the lotus, one should meditate on the syllable <term>Pra</term>, which is the nature of <term>Prajnaparamita</term> <gloss>The Perfection of Wisdom</gloss>. Then, imagine the white syllable <term>Kham</term> from the direction of the sky, which has the nature of <term>Vairocana</term>, coming and dwelling in the center of the lotus. Then, from the lotus, the syllable <term>Pra</term>, and the syllable <term>Kham</term> becoming one, one should imagine the generation of <term>Sumeru</term> <gloss>The Great Mountain</gloss>, the king of mountains. 

Reciting <term>Om Dridho Me Bhava Raksha Sarvam Svaha</term> <gloss>Om, Be firm for me, protect everything, Svaha</gloss>, one should bless the mountain as having the nature of a vajra by touching the ground with the extended vajra-fist gesture. Upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, through the <term>mudra</term> of the causal vajra, one should emanate a peaked vajra and a tiered palace made of jewels. 

There, in the station of <term>Vairocana</term>, from <term>A Sim A</term> <note>seed syllables associated with the lion throne</note>, a lion throne appears. དམ་ཚིག་འཛིན་པ་པོ། །ཞེས་བྱ་བ་འདི་དང་། ཨོཾ་བཛྲ་བནྡྷ་ཧཾ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་འདིས། རང་གི་དམ་ཚིག་ལ་སྦྱར་བར་བྱའོ། །ཕྱག་རྒྱ་སྦྱར་ཞིང་འདི་སྐད་ཅེས་བརྗོད་པར་བྱ་སྟེ། མངོན་པར་འདོད་པར་གྱིས་ཤིག་ཅེས་བརྗོད་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ལ་ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ནི་འདི་ཡིན་ཏེ། རྡོ་རྗེ་སྲུང་བ་དམ་བཅིངས་ལ། །རྡོ་རྗེ་
བསྡམས་པ་དེས་མནན་པས། །འདི་ནི་སྲུང་བའི་དམ་ཚིག་སྟེ། །སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་བསྲུང་བའོ། །སླར་ཡང་སྔགས་པས་མཆོད་ཡོན་ཕུལ་ནས། ལན་གསུམ་གྱི་བར་དུ་འཐོར་འཐུང་བྱས་པས། རྡོ་རྗེ་གནོད་སྦྱིན་གྱི་བཟླས་པའི་ཆུས་ལན་གསུམ་གྱི་བར་དུ་བསངས་ཏེ། རྡོ་རྗེ་སྲུང་བའི་ཕྱག་
རྒྱས་ཡང་དག་པར་བསྲུངས་ལ། མཆོད་པ་རྣམ་པ་ལྔས་མཆོད་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ནས་སྒེག་མོ་ལ་སོགས་པའི་མཆོད་པ་བཞིས་ཡང་དག་པར་མཆོད་ལ། ལས་དང་རྗེས་སུ་མཐུན་པའི་མེ་ལ་རང་གི་སྔགས་ཀྱིས་མར་གྱི་སྲེག་བླུགས་གསུམ་དགང་གཟར་གྱིས་དབུལ་བར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ནས་བགེགས་
ཡོད་མེད་བརྟག་པར་བྱའོ། །དེ་ལ་ལས་དང་རྗེས་སུ་མཐུན་པར་བརྗོད་པ་ནི་འདི་ཡིན་ཏེ། དེ་ལ་ཞི་བ་བྱེད་ན། ལན་གསུམ་གྱི་བར་དུ་ཁྲུས་བྱ་བ་སྔོན་དུ་འགྲོ་བས། གོས་དཀར་པོ་མ་ཉམས་པའི་སྟོད་གཡོགས་དང་། སྨད་གཡོགས་བགོས་ཏེ། སྙིང་བརྩེ་བ་དང་། དུལ་བ་དང་། ཚངས་པར་སྤྱོད་
པས་ཁ་ཤར་ཕྱོགས་སུ་བལྟས་ཏེ། འཇམ་པའི་སྟན་འབོལ་བའམ། པདྨའི་སྟན་ལ་འདུག་སྟེ། ཙནྡན་དཀར་པོ་དྲི་ཞིམ་པོ་དང་། མེ་ཏོག་དཀར་པོ་དང་། ཙནྡན་གྱི་བདུག་པ་དང་། བ་དཀར་མོའི་མར་དང་། དཀར་གསུམ་གྱི་ལྷ་བཤོས་དང་། བྱང་ཆུབ་མཆོག་གི་ཕྱག་རྒྱས་དགང་གཟར་བླངས་ལ། 
ཞི་བའི་ཉམས་དང་ལྡན་པས་མེའི་ལྷ་ཁ་དོག་དཀར་པོའི་གཟུགས་ཅན་བསམས་ལ། མར་གྱི་དགང་བླུགས་གསུམ་མེ་ལ་དབུལ་བར་བྱའོ། །རྒྱས་པ་ལ་ནི་དགའ་ཞིང་མགུ་བའི་གཟུགས་ཅན་མདོག་སེར་པོ། རྒྱན་སེར་པོ་དང་ལྡན་པའི་མེའི་ལྷ་བསམས་ལ། རང་གི་ལུས་དྲང་པོས་སྣ་ཚོགས་

Reciting <term>Om hana samaya hum phat</term> <gloss>Om, strike the pledge, Hum Phat</gloss>, one should say, "You must do whatever I say," and place them under the pledge through the application of a <term>mudra</term> <gloss>symbolic hand gesture</gloss>. Regarding that, this is the <term>mudra</term>:

Form the <term>vajrasattva-mudra</term> <gloss>gesture of the diamond being</gloss> firmly, pressing between the two thumbs. With the little fingers at the tips of the <term>vajra</term> <gloss>ritual scepter</gloss>, one holds the sharp pledge.

By this, and the mantra <term>Om vajra bandha ham</term> <gloss>Om, diamond bond, Ham</gloss>, one should bind them to one's own pledge. While applying the <term>mudra</term>, one should say these words: "Act according to your desires!" Regarding that, this is the <term>mudra</term>:

Having firmly bound the <term>vajra</term> protection, and pressing with that <term>vajra</term> bond, this is the pledge of protection, which protects all sentient beings.

Furthermore, after the <term>tantrika</term> <gloss>practitioner of the tantras</gloss> has offered the <term>argham</term> <gloss>ceremonial water for the mouth</gloss>, they should perform the sprinkling and sipping three times. Having purified three times with water consecrated by the recitation of <term>Vajrayaksa</term> <gloss>The Diamond Spirit</gloss>, and having protected thoroughly with the <term>mudra</term> of <term>vajra</term> protection, one should make offerings with the five types of offerings <note>these typically include flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, and food</note>. Then, one should offer correctly with the four offerings of <term>Lasya</term> <gloss>The Goddess of Charm</gloss> and the others. One should offer three ladles of butter into the fire that accords with the specific ritual activity, using one's own mantra. Then, one should examine whether or not there are obstructing spirits.

Regarding the description of what accords with the ritual activity: if one is performing a ritual of pacification <note>a rite to calm sickness, negativity, or obstacles</note>, it should be preceded by bathing three times. One should wear pristine white upper and lower garments. With a compassionate heart, being disciplined and observing celibacy, one should face east. Sitting on a soft, comfortable cushion or a lotus seat, one should take the <term>gang-zar</term> <gloss>ceremonial pouring ladle</gloss> with the <term>mudra</term> of supreme enlightenment. Use white sandalwood of pleasing fragrance, white flowers, sandalwood incense, butter from a white cow, and deity-food made of the three whites <note>milk, curd, and butter</note>. Possessing a peaceful demeanor, meditate on the Fire God as having a white-colored form, and offer three ladles of butter into the fire.
